plain: The two exits (a recorded, changeable grid; gravity as a strongly interacting or non-local pattern) are not two separate doors with no tests. Bounded necessary-condition tests exist and I ran three: a periodic recorded grid keeps its cubic anisotropy and carries the metric only as a density of records (exit C), graded lengths are the finite-slot wall (T64), and only an aperiodic state is new, replacing the Lattice axiom wholesale; the non-local exit needs a partner-gapping kernel whose range grows with the wavelength. No graviton was found or excluded.
best_route: R4 misframing: replace 'find a model' by a necessary-condition battery (ground-state isotropy, polarisation content, kernel range), then settle T77 (are exact balance laws outputs of directed formation).
test: Ran isotropy (step-count norm anisotropy 1.41 in the 26-star, Poisson graphs isotropic to 1%), diluted-Z3 metric density (rank 6, linear to 5%; a fixed polarisation is 40/40/20 percent TT/helicity 1/helicity 0) and a non-local kernel truncation (rho ~ 1 for R<=4; needs R ~ 4/|q|, tail r^-3.07).
cheaper_question: Which ground state does recorded adjacency choose (periodic grid, graded lengths, or aperiodic), since each lands in an already-named wall; and can exit C's tensor balance law be an output of directed local formation (T77)?
